# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 25 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 25 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_025_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 25

**25:1** And there arose a great consternation among the priests when Zechariah had not appeared at the appointed time to carry out his service before God. So a vessel of water was brought and a prayer was offered, that God might make known what had happened. And they cast lots, and the lot fell to Simeon.

**25:2** Now Simeon had been told by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had first seen the Christ incarnate. And when the child was brought to the temple, he saw him and recognized him, and said: "Lord, now let your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation."

**25:3** And it was I, James, who wrote this history in Jerusalem. And when the tumult arose at the death of Herod, I withdrew into the wilderness until the commotion had ceased, giving glory to the Lord God, who gave me this grace and this wisdom.

**25:4** Peace be to the one who fears the Lord. Amen.

---

*[Scribal colophon — P.Bodmer V:] The Birth of Mary. Revelation of James. Peace to the one who sent it and to the one who reads it.*

---

## Translator's Note

Chapter 25 appears to be a supplementary passage in many MSS, completing or recapitulating the material of ch. 23-24. P.Bodmer V (the oldest witness) treats what we call chs. 24 and 25 as a continuous closing section. The Simeon scene (25:2) quotes Luke 2:29 and 2:30 virtually verbatim, confirming the Protevangelium's knowledge of Luke. The final scribal colophon — preserved in P.Bodmer V — gives the ancient title of the text: "The Birth of Mary, Revelation of James." This is the earliest known title. The double peace blessing ("Peace to the one who sent it and to the one who reads it") is a standard Coptic and Greek scribal formula, suggesting the manuscript passed between communities as a cherished text.
